seoTitle: Shivantika Saxena: therapy site with booking
description: How I turned Shivantika Saxena's draft into a live counselling practice site: clients book on Cal.com's free plan and pay her by UPI, with no gateway fee.
deck: Her draft had a warm editorial look and no way to book; now clients book on their own and pay her by UPI.
summary: A counselling psychologist sent me her one file HTML draft. It had a warm editorial look, placeholders where her details belonged, and no way for clients to book.

I rebuilt it as plain files any host can serve, then moved it closer to her own design document, version by version. Clients book on Cal.com's free plan and pay her by UPI with no gateway, and a paid session waits until she confirms the money landed. A script set up both session types, so her side of the setup became 7 short steps.
Her own calendar was wired into the page 4 days after my first commit. No gateway takes ₹35.40 of each ₹1,500 fee, modelled at Razorpay's standard 2% plus 18% GST on that 2%.

offer.who: Solo practitioners, such as therapists, coaches and tutors, who have a draft or a clear idea for their site and no way for clients to book.
offer.gets: A one page site in your own look and words. Self serve booking on a free scheduler plan, with your intake questions asked before the first call. Payment by UPI with no gateway fee, each paid slot held until you confirm. A WhatsApp or email line in case the calendar fails, and copy that makes no outcome claims.
offer.needs: Your draft or brief, your palette and copy, a Cal.com account connected to Google Calendar and Google Meet, and your UPI ID.
offer.setup: I write the site and a script that sets up your sessions, limits and intake questions. Your part is a short list of steps, with a direct link to each screen you need. Here, her own calendar was wired into the page a few days after my first commit.

Commit times, not deploy times.

The practice's public Cal.com pages, read on 25 Oct 2026 without booking anything: two visible session types, Free Initial Consultation (20 minutes, confirmed at once) and Therapy Session (50 minutes, needs her confirmation, Google Meet, a rolling booking window of 7 days on Asia/Kolkata time, stored as ROLLING_WINDOW). Before: her draft had no booking (project notes), and my first commit's booking section rendered as an empty box.

The Cal.com setup guide kept in the site's repository, in two versions: the first (commit 973718b, 6 Aug 2026) has 16 checklist lines, 2 of them optional, and 6 booking questions to type by hand; the current one (commit 54dac92, the same day) has 7 steps, 6 of them with a direct link into Cal.com and 1 a message to me, and estimates about 5 minutes. Lines counted on 25 Oct 2026. The minutes are the guide's estimate, not a timing.

Razorpay pricing page, read 25 Oct 2026: 2% per transaction plus GST, and the same 2% platform fee on UPI payments taken through the gateway; new accounts were offered 0% for their first 90 days. Her fee of ₹1,500 a session is from her site. Model: ₹1,500 × 2% = ₹30; GST of 18% on ₹30 = ₹5.40; ₹35.40 a session.

Headless Chromium render of the live site on 25 Oct 2026: 0 forms and 0 input, textarea or select elements. Response headers read the same day: frame options, content type options, referrer policy, permissions policy and strict transport security; no content security policy.
Cal.com pricing page, read 25 Oct 2026: the Individuals plan is free, with unlimited event types and templated workflows.

My first commit (6230e23, 3 Aug 2026), rendered in headless Chromium on 25 Oct 2026: the booking section is an empty box with placeholder WhatsApp and email links. 30 placeholder slots counted by pattern in its index.html (bracketed fields plus placeholder domain, phone, email and handle values: 29 single line matches and 1 that wraps a line), plus a placeholder booking link in main.js.
Razorpay's pricing explainer, published 13 Feb 2026 and read 25 Oct 2026: GST at 18% applies to the platform fee only.

Calendly pricing page, read 25 Oct 2026: Free includes one event type and leaves out automated reminders; Standard costs $10 per seat per month billed yearly, or $12 billed monthly. Model: 12 × $10 = $120 and 12 × $12 = $144 a year for one seat. US dollars as listed; no conversion made.

The project notes kept with the site's code, not published, written during the build: payment first planned as a prepaid gateway; her answers of 6 Aug 2026 (UPI with no gateway, two session types, 15 minutes after each, 4 a day, a week ahead, a 24 hour email reminder); Cal.com chosen for its free reminder workflows; her 3 hand made duplicate session types hidden through the API, not deleted; colours first sampled from her document's pixels (Linen read as #f0e7de, Tea Rose as #ecb4b3), then replaced by the exact #EEE7DD and #EBB4B2 from her PDF; her rules of no dashes and two typefaces; the site live on Vercel since 5 Aug 2026, with no domain bought yet.

The setup script kept in the site's repository (90 lines, Cal.com API v2, Node's built in fetch), read 25 Oct 2026: 7 settings on the consultation (title, address, length, description, Google Meet, intake questions, 15 minutes after) and 10 on the paid session (the same 7, plus at most 4 a day, a 7 day rolling window and a confirmation policy that keeps the slot held while pending), 17 in all, with 6 intake questions on each. Cal.com rejects a second event at the same address, so a rerun only prints that refusal for each one.

Commit 3d4a802 (24 Sep 2026) and headless renders on 25 Oct 2026: just before that commit, index.html held 13 em or en dashes and 12 hyphenated compounds in its visible text, title and meta; the live index.html holds 0 in the same places, the viewport meta aside. Fonts loaded: Courier Prime, Fraunces and Mulish at commit b4c4fbd; Fraunces and Mulish live.

The site's own files, read 25 Oct 2026: wc -c of index.html, styles.css, main.js, favicon.svg and three SVG drawings gives 29,804 bytes, with no framework and no build step; the README says any static host works. main.js loads Calendly or Cal.com from one BOOKING_URL value and leaves only the WhatsApp and email line when it is empty (lines 14 to 23); index.html keeps that line under the calendar, with a note for readers without JavaScript (lines 199 to 211); .gitignore keeps env files out of git, and the setup script reads its key from the environment.

draft.h2: Her draft had a design, but no booking
draft.lede: She sent me one HTML file: an editorial layout, a warm palette and a CBT thought record card in the hero. Every detail was a placeholder, and clients had no way to book.
p: I kept the calendar choice open, with one line that could load Calendly or Cal.com, until I understood how a session should work for her: which sessions, how long, how many a day, a gap after each, how far ahead, the reminder, and how she takes money. Her answers on 6 Aug 2026 became the settings in the path above.
I kept her look and rebuilt it as plain files that any host can serve. My first commit, on 3 Aug 2026, still had

gateway.h2: The gateway she did not need

turn.expected: A prepaid booking: Calendly for the calendar and a payment gateway, such as Stripe or Razorpay, for the fee. My own notes from the first days called it the likely fit.
turn.cost: A gateway keeps a share of every fee, UPI payments included. Calendly's free plan allows one session type and no automatic reminders, and she wanted two session types and a reminder the day before.

costMetric.label: a session to Razorpay at its standard rate: 2% of her ₹1,500 fee, plus 18% GST on that 2%.

moreMetrics.label: a year for Calendly Standard, one seat: $10 a month billed yearly, or $12 billed monthly.

turn.line: She already took UPI. The booking only had to wait for her.
turn.built: Cal.com's free plan, which allows both session types and templated reminders. The paid session asks for her confirmation: the client books, pays her by UPI, and she confirms when the money lands. I set the slot to stay held meanwhile, so nobody else can take it. The free consult confirms at once.

p: The hard part was never the calendar. It was asking how she already took payment, which removed the gateway, and finding the setting that holds a slot until she confirms. After that the work was listening: her document set the order, her PDF set the colours, and her rules now sit in the notes where the next edit will find them.
